title: Proactive Agents – Kath Korevec, Google Labs
talk_summary: Kath Korevec (Google Labs, Jules) argues async coding agents fail because humans still babysit them, and proposes proactive agents that observe the repo, learn preferences, and act at the right moment. She describes Jules features: repo indexing to surface TODOs/best-practice fixes with confidence scores, a memory store, an adversarial critic agent, Playwright screenshot verification, and just-in-time context cheat sheets.

takeaways.technique: Repo-indexed proactive work discovery with confidence tiers
takeaways.what_they_do: On enable, Jules indexes the whole repo, finds TODOs, missing tests, unused deps, unsafe patterns, and presents candidate tasks ranked high/medium/low confidence with rationale and code location, so the human clicks to start instead of writing prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Jules will index your entire code base... it's found a bunch of to-dos... the signal is high confidence, medium confidence, and low

takeaways.technique: Adversarial critic agent doing full code review
takeaways.what_they_do: A separate critic agent works adversarially against the coding agent to enforce quality and perform a complete code review, rather than the author agent self-checking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We've added a critic agent which works adversarially with Jewels to make sure that the code is is high quality, but then also does a full code review.

takeaways.technique: Agent-written Playwright verification with screenshot fed back into trajectory
takeaways.what_they_do: Jules writes a Playwright script, runs it, takes a screenshot, and inserts that screenshot back into the agent trajectory so the result is validated visually rather than asserted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Jules will write a playwright script, take a screenshot, and then put that back into the trajectory for you to validate.

takeaways.what_they_do: Jules writes its own memories about the project, and both the agent and the human can edit or interact with them, building persistent project context over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's the ability for Jewels to write its own memories and you can edit them and interact with them.

takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent gets stuck on a specific recurring operation, it consults a pre-written cheat sheet immediately instead of escalating to the human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's like a Jules cheat sheet where if it's doing something very specific it can and get stuck it can just immediately look at that cheat sheet instead of reaching out to you.

takeaways.technique: Cross-agent signal convergence with human in the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Separate agents (code, design, data) each observe a different signal and jointly propose improvements, while the human observes, refines, and redirects rather than approving every step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Jewels can see what's breaking in the software, Stitch understands how users are interacting with it, and Insights connects behaviors from real world signals
